newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish paper calls for Clinton apology over baby.
newsitem.headline: Danish paper calls for Clinton apology over baby.

text.p: A Danish newspaper on Thursday quoted a child psychiatrist as saying a baby forcibly removed from her Danish mother by New York authorities for four days could be traumatised and called on President Bill Clinton to apologise when he visits Denmark in July.

The BT tabloid, with a front-page headline reading "Back with mother after four-day nightmare," quoted local hospital consultant Gideon Zlotnik as saying that New York officials rather than actress Annette Sorensen were guilty of neglect.

"We know from several scientific studies that children in the 8-24 month age group are extremely vulnerable to the effects of being suddenly removed from their mother, father or other person to whom they are attached," he said.

"I know that in the United States they generally let mothers have their small children with them in jail, in special sections. They are usually very aware of the harmful consequences of separating mother and child."
Authorities took Liv from her mother and American father, Exavier Wardlaw, on Saturday. The couple had left her outside an East Village restaurant while watching her through the window, police said.
Passers-by said the baby was cold and crying and called police, they added.
The family was reunited on Wednesday but the parents face charges of endangering the welfare of a child and disorderly conduct.
Sorensen and Wardlaw are due in Criminal Court on Monday, and she must return to Family Court after that for a hearing on custody of the child. Sorensen has already spent two days in jail.

Parents in Denmark, where street crime usually means riding a bicycle on the pavement, commonly leave children outside shops or restaurants where they can keep an eye on their infants through a window.
In a separate article, the paper said that Sorensen would have been foolish to leave 14-month-old daughter Liv outside a restaurant but police and welfare authorities had overeacted.
"Naturally you don't let a 14-month-old child wait alone in a push-chair outside a restaurant. You have to be either Danish or an idiot not to understand that," it wrote.
"But you have to be American with a capital A to understand and accept that a 30-year-old Danish mother can be slapped in handcuffs, thrown in jail and separated from her child."

It said that U.S. President Bill Clinton's wife, Hilary had written about "wonderful Denmark, where children in their prams can be left on the street", and suggested that his planned July visit to Copenhagen would be a chance to make ammends.
"Dear Clinton, if you are a decent person you should bring a big apology with you on your visit," BT wrote.
